quest.title: For Fruits, Seeds, and Trees
quest.description: When you wake up, Festival Utsava is no more, and Arama is nowhere to be found. Only the faint fragrance from the garland tells you that this was not a dream.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x350, Primogem x40, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x5

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Arama!

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: #Nara {NICKNAME}, Paimon, you seem fresh, like fresh Zaytun Peaches. But Paimon looks unhappy. Did you have a nightmare?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon was afraid you'd abandoned us!

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: Why would you think that? I've been here the whole time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: B—Because Vanarana is in a dream, and the fun we had at Festival Utsava was like a dream... Paimon was afraid that everything would all go away once we woke up...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We'd be all that's left, just like when we first started the journey...

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: But the things that happen in dreams are real. I have observed Nara before and found that nightmares would make them timid, and that nice dreams would make them happy, just like things that happen outside their dreams.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: So when Paimon dreamed of meeting us and also dreamed of meeting Vanarana, Paimon, it was as real as doing both in reality.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: That's right! I'm here waiting for you to go to the Fane of Ashvattha together, to get the Bija, and to make Narana feel better.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #...That's true. Bah, {NICKNAME}, you must have put weird mushrooms in the feast to make Paimon think about such stuff.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's go, then!

choices.text: And we still have to help Rana.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Yes, we have to go to the Fane of Ashvattha to get the Bija, and to make Narana feel better!

choices.text: Don't get in your own head, Paimon. Let's go.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: That's right. We've got to go to the Fane of Ashvattha to get the Bija so Narana can get better!

talks.objective: Go to the Fane of Ashvattha
Go to the Fane of Ashvattha

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: #Wonderful, this place isn't corroded by Marana like Arayama and the others were! Nara {NICKNAME}, Paimon, this is the Ashvattha Tree.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, what a weird-looking tree...

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: That's rude, Paimon! You'll make the Ashvattha Tree mad! This is a very, very mighty tree — the oldest Vasara Tree there is. Even older than any Aranara and their stories...

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: Queen Aranyani sang here — thousands of moons ago, or perhaps even more. She had just left Valuka at the time, and the woods weren't as lush as now, so there was still lots of sand on the ground.

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: Her Ararakalari was more powerful than any Aranara's, since her song was the closest to the Sourcesong. So Ashvattha responded to her call and sprouted from Sarva.

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: Queen Aranyani told Ashvattha that there were many smart, beautiful, yet lonely Nara in the woods and that the children of the forest must increase so that they might become friends with the Nara.

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: Therefore, Ashvattha produced a beautiful and full pomegranate with many seeds inside, the first of which to sprout was Aramuhukunda.

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: That made Aramuhukunda the very first Aranara. Later, all the seeds grew and Aranara spread like leaves on a tree. We and Nara were both people of the forest.

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: That's why the Ashvattha Tree is very powerful and very important! Just like Nara bear Nara children, all Aranara are progeny of Ashvattha and Queen Aranyani.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So that's how it is... Sorry, Arama. The Ashvattha Tree is super impressive!

choices.text: How rude of you, Paimon, calling someone's mother weird like that.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon didn't mean to! Anyway, what do we need to do now to get the Bija?

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Right. Just like trees need earth and rain to flourish, dreams and memories are what a Vasara Tree needs. As I mentioned a moment ago, the Ashvattha Tree is the oldest of the Vasara Trees.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: That's why we've brought three Vasoma Fruits from Araji, Arayama, and Aramaha as offerings for the Ashvattha Tree to bear great fruit.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Araji, Arayama, and Aramaha's Vasoma Fruits? Don't you mean the fruits of the Vasara Trees?

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: That's what they are, yes.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #Stand closer to the Ashvattha Tree, Nara {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa...

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Yes, all Aranara are descendants of this tree. You're now connected to all Aranara, and you bear their blessings, and so the Ashvattha Tree shall bless you too.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: For as long as you wear this garland, the Ashvattha Tree will recognize you as a child of the forest.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Mmm...

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Something's wrong with the Ashvattha Tree. It feels a bit weak... This must be because of the Marana that's been showing up everywhere lately.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Regardless, we're going into the Ashvattha Tree's dream next, and we'll offer the Vasoma Fruits to the Tree of Dreams. That should rejuvenate it!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #So we're doing this like we did back in Ashvattha's Concourses, right? {NICKNAME} will reach out and "Woosh," we'll be in the dream!

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #Yes. Very smart, Paimon. So if you're ready, Nara {NICKNAME}, reach your hand out and let's enter the Ashvattha Tree's dream.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Arama just mentioned Marana... Paimon wonders what we'll see in this dream! Oh well, it's fine! We've got {NICKNAME} around, after all!

choices.text: Give me some time to ready myself.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Sure. Let me know when you're ready. I'll go with you!

choices.text: Give me some time to get ready.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Sure. Let me know when you're ready. I'll go with you!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Finally we are here. Huh... Paimon remembers that we could see this mysterious tree in other Vasara Trees' dreams as well!

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: #I'm sorry, Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon. It escaped me that Marana has also corroded the Ashvattha Tree's dream...

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: Countless black pests are corroding the roots of the Tree of Dreams in Sarva. I can feel Marana's hands, shaking the dream to its core.

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: Sorry... I should have known this would've been the case when we saw Marana in Ashvattha's Concourses before.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #It's okay! We fixed this easily with {NICKNAME} around, didn't we?

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #The Vasoma Fruits should at least restore some of his power. I'm counting on you, Nara {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Yes, I understand. I didn't think it would be so soon, but I'm aware that I'll know what to do when the time comes.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Just like the clouds know that they must release rain, and the rain knows that it must fall to the ground, seeds know that they must grow into big trees and bear lots of plump fruits.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Something's weird about Arama...

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Oh, I was just speaking to the Tree of Dreams. Huh, so you couldn't hear it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's seen Aranakin talking to mushrooms before... But people can't normally communicate with plants, you know?

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: I see! I just learned something new. Thank you, Paimon.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #Don't worry about the Bija, Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon. Let's just leave the dream for now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But... Will what happened here affect the Bija in any way?

choices.text: Well, it wasn't as easy as Paimon made it sound...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, you did it regardless, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But... Will what happened here affect the Bija in any way?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The heart of the Ashvattha Tree is glowing... Is that the Bija?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It hasn't been easy, but Rana can finally be healed!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!?

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: The Ashvattha Tree has been corroded by Marana and cannot bear any Bija. I have to plant a new Ashvattha Tree in order to help you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But won't it require a long time to grow from a seed to a tree?

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Don't worry, the speed of a Vasara Tree's growth has to do with its seed. The Ashvattha Tree has given me all its power, and with the Vasoma Fruits and our shared memory, it will be fine.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Thank you, the first Ashvattha Tree. Thank you, Araji, Arayama, and Aramaha. I will utilize your memories to rebuild the path between the new Ashvattha Tree and the dreams.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Do you get the feeling that Arama's different now...

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Am I? I learned a lot of new things, figured out lots of new words, and obtained a lot of memories.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: But rest assured, I'm still me, your friend. I will help you for sure.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Old Vanarana is sealed deep within the Fane of Ashvattha. That's where we'll find Marana's Avatar.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: It will imbue the land and Sarva with viper venom until everything green turns brown, every flower has withered, every brook is putrid, and every creature is dead.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: We must destroy it. Only then can a tree strong enough to produce the Bija grow.

choices.text: I believe you. What do we do now?

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #So long as you understand, Nara {NICKNAME}, it's all good.

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: How did this...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why would The Withering be in the Ashvattha Tree's dream?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Regardless, we've got to get rid of The Withering as soon as possible!
